shortDescription: Add or remove PostgreSQL databases from a remote host

options.name: ca_cert
options.description: Specifies the name of a file containing SSL certificate authority (CA) certificate(s). If the file exists, the server's certificate will be verified to be signed by one of these authorities.

options.name: comment
options.description: Sets a comment on the database. To reset the comment, pass an empty string.

options.name: conn_limit
options.description: Specifies the database connection limit.

options.name: connect_params
options.description: Any additional parameters to be passed to libpg. These parameters take precedence.

options.name: dump_extra_args
options.description: Provides additional arguments when I(state) is C(dump). Cannot be used with dump-file-format-related arguments like ``--format=d``.

options.name: encoding
options.description: Encoding of the database.

options.name: force
options.description: Used to forcefully drop a database when the I(state) is C(absent), ignored otherwise.

options.name: icu_locale
options.description: Specifies the ICU locale (ICU_LOCALE) for the database default collation order and character classification, overriding the setting locale. The locale provider must be ICU. The default is the setting of locale if specified; otherwise the same setting as the template database.

options.name: lc_collate
options.description: Collation order (LC_COLLATE) to use in the database must match collation order of template database unless C(template0) is used as template.

options.name: lc_ctype
options.description: Character classification (LC_CTYPE) to use in the database (e.g. lower, upper, ...). Must match LC_CTYPE of template database unless C(template0) is used as template.

options.name: locale_provider
options.description: Specifies the provider to use for the default collation in this database (LOCALE_PROVIDER). Possible values are icu (if the server was built with ICU support) or libc. By default, the provider is the same as that of the template.

options.name: login_host
options.description: Host running the database. If you have connection issues when using C(localhost), try to use C(127.0.0.1) instead.

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password this module should use to establish its PostgreSQL session.

options.name: login_port
options.description: Database port to connect to. The C(port) alias is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release. Use C(login_port) instead.

options.name: login_unix_socket
options.description: Path to a Unix domain socket for local connections.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The username this module should use to establish its PostgreSQL session.

options.name: maintenance_db
options.description: The value specifies the initial database (which is also called as maintenance DB) that Ansible connects to.

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the database to add or remove.

options.name: owner
options.description: Name of the role to set as owner of the database.

options.name: session_role
options.description: Switch to session_role after connecting. The specified session_role must be a role that the current login_user is a member of. Permissions checking for SQL commands is carried out as though the session_role were the one that had logged in originally.

options.name: ssl_cert
options.description: Specifies the file name of the client SSL certificate.

options.name: ssl_key
options.description: Specifies the location for the secret key used for the client certificate.

options.name: ssl_mode
options.description: Determines whether or with what priority a secure SSL TCP/IP connection will be negotiated with the server. See U(https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/static/libpq-ssl.html) for more information on the modes. Default of C(prefer) matches libpq default.

options.name: state
options.description: The database state. C(present) implies that the database should be created if necessary. C(absent) implies that the database should be removed if present. C(dump) requires a target definition to which the database will be backed up. (Added in Ansible 2.4) Note that in some PostgreSQL versions of pg_dump, which is an embedded PostgreSQL utility and is used by the module, returns rc 0 even when errors occurred (e.g. the connection is forbidden by pg_hba.conf, etc.), so the module returns changed=T

options.name: tablespace
options.description: The tablespace to set for the database U(https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-alterdatabase.html). If you want to move the database back to the default tablespace, explicitly set this to pg_default.

options.name: target
options.description: File to back up or restore from. Used when I(state) is C(dump) or C(restore).

options.name: target_opts
options.description: Additional arguments for pg_dump or restore program (pg_restore or psql, depending on target's format). Used when I(state) is C(dump) or C(restore).

options.name: template
options.description: Template used to create the database.

options.name: trust_input
options.description: If C(false), check whether values of parameters I(owner), I(conn_limit), I(encoding), I(db), I(template), I(tablespace), I(session_role) are potentially dangerous. It makes sense to use C(false) only when SQL injections via the parameters are possible.
